question: Kumaradevi, a Lichchhavi princess, was married to whom among the following Gupta kings?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Chandragupta I**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Kumaradevi, a Lichchhavi princess, was married to Chandragupta I, the third ruler of the Gupta dynasty.
 
• This matrimonial alliance significantly strengthened the position and power of the Gupta dynasty.
 
• Chandragupta I ruled from approximately 320 CE to 335 CE and laid the foundation for the Gupta Empire's golden age.
 
• The marriage to Kumaradevi, and the subsequent alliance with the Lichchhavis, helped Chandragupta I to extend his influence over the Ganges River basin.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Chandragupta I**

 
 
• He was the third ruler of the Gupta dynasty and succeeded his father, Ghatotkacha.
 
• His reign marked the beginning of the Gupta Era, which is considered a classical age in Indian history known for its extensive achievements in arts, architecture, science, and literature.
 
• Chandragupta I assumed the title of Maharajadhiraja (King of Kings), indicating his supreme status.
 
 
 
• **Lichchhavi**
 
 
• The Lichchhavis were an influential clan in ancient India, based in the region of present-day Bihar.
 
• They are mentioned in various ancient Indian texts, including the Buddhist and Jain scriptures.
 
• Their political and military alliance with the Guptas through the marriage of Kumaradevi to Chandragupta I played a crucial role in the rise of the Gupta Empire.
 
 
 
• **Gupta Dynasty**
 
 
• The Gupta dynasty is known as the "Golden Age" of India due to its advancements in science, mathematics, astronomy, religion, and philosophy.
 
• It was founded by Sri Gupta and reached its zenith under the rule of Chandragupta I, Samudragupta, and Chandragupta II.
 
• The period saw the creation of notable works such as the Kama Sutra, the development of the decimal system, and the flourishing of classical Sanskrit literature.
 
 
 
• **Matrimonial Alliances in Ancient India**
 
 
• Matrimonial alliances were a common political strategy used by ancient Indian rulers to strengthen their position and forge alliances with other powerful clans and kingdoms.
 
• Such alliances often brought peace and stability, as well as mutual economic and military benefits.
 
• The alliance between the Guptas and the Lichchhavis is one of the most notable examples of this practice.
